questions.text: If $\mathrm{Z}=\frac{\mathrm{A}^{2} \mathrm{~B}^{3}}{\mathrm{C}^{4}}$, then the relative error in Z will be :

options.D:
$\frac{\Delta \mathrm{A}}{\mathrm{A}}+\frac{\Delta \mathrm{B}}{\mathrm{B}}-\frac{\Delta \mathrm{C}}{\mathrm{C}}$

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)
Sol. $\mathrm{Z}=\frac{\mathrm{A}^{2} \mathrm{~B}^{3}}{\mathrm{C}^{4}}$
In case of error
$$\begin{array}{l}
\frac{d Z}{Z}=\frac{2 d A}{A}+\frac{3 d B}{B}+\frac{4 d C}{C} \\
\frac{\Delta Z}{Z}=\frac{2 \Delta A}{A}+\frac{3 \Delta B}{B}+\frac{4 \Delta C}{C}
\end{array}$$

questions.text: $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{A}}$ is a vector quantity such that $|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{A}}|=$ nonzero constant. Which of the following expressions is true for $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{A}}$ ?

options.D:
$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{A}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{A}}>0$

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)
Sol. $|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{A}}| \neq 0$
$$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{A}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{A}}=|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{A}}||\overrightarrow{\mathrm{A}}| \sin 0^{\circ} \hat{\mathrm{n}}=0$$

questions.text: Which of the following relations is true for two unit vectors $\hat{\mathrm{A}}$ and $\hat{\mathrm{B}}$ making an angle $\theta$ to each other?

options.D:
$|\hat{\mathrm{A}}-\hat{\mathrm{B}}|=|\hat{\mathrm{A}}+\hat{\mathrm{B}}| \cos \frac{\theta}{2}$

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol.
$$\begin{array}{l}
|\hat{\mathrm{A}}+\hat{\mathrm{B}}|=\sqrt{|\hat{\mathrm{A}}|^{2}+|\hat{\mathrm{B}}|^{2}+2|\hat{\mathrm{~A}} \| \hat{\mathrm{B}}| \cos \theta} \\
=\sqrt{1+1+2 \cos \theta} \\
=\sqrt{2(1+\cos \theta)} \\
=\sqrt{2 \times 2 \cos ^{2} \frac{\theta}{2}} \\
=2 \cos \frac{\theta}{2} \\
|\hat{\mathrm{~A}}-\hat{\mathrm{B}}|=\sqrt{|\hat{\mathrm{A}}|^{2}+|\hat{\mathrm{B}}|^{2}-2|\hat{\mathrm{~A}} \| \hat{\mathrm{B}}| \cos \theta} \\
=\sqrt{2-2 \cos \theta} \\
=2 \sin \frac{\theta}{2} \\
\frac{|\hat{\mathrm{~A}}+\hat{\mathrm{B}}|}{|\hat{\mathrm{A}}-\hat{\mathrm{B}}|}=\cot \frac{\theta}{2}
\end{array}$$

questions.text: If force $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}}=3 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+4 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-2 \hat{\mathrm{k}}$ acts on a particle having position vector $2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{k}}$ then, the torque about the origin will be :-

options.D:
$10 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}-5 \hat{\mathrm{k}}$

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol. $\vec{\tau}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\
2 & 1 & 2 \\
3 & 4 & -2
\end{array}\right| \\
=\hat{i}(-2-8)-\hat{j}(-4-6)+\hat{k}(8-3) \\
=-10 \hat{i}+10 \hat{j}+5 \hat{k}
\end{array}$$

questions.text: The height of any point P above the surface of earth is equal to diameter of earth. The value of acceleration due to gravity at point P will be : (Given $\mathrm{g}=$ acceleration due to gravity at the surface of earth)

options.D:
g/9

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)
Sol. $\mathrm{g}=\frac{\mathrm{Gm}}{\mathrm{r}^{2}}$
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{g}^{\prime} & =\frac{\mathrm{Gm}}{(3 \mathrm{r})^{2}} \\
\mathrm{~g}^{\prime} & =\frac{\mathrm{Gm}}{9 \mathrm{r}^{2}} \\
\mathrm{~g}^{\prime} & =\frac{\mathrm{g}}{9}
\end{aligned}$$

questions.text: The relation between root mean square speed $\left(\mathrm{v}_{\text {rms }}\right)$ and most probable speed $\left(\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{p}}\right)$ for the molar mass M of oxygen gas molecule at the temperature of 300 K will be :-

options.D:
$\mathrm{v}_{\text {rms }}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{3}} \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{p}}$

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol. $\mathrm{v}_{\text {rms }}=\sqrt{\frac{3 \mathrm{RT}}{\mathrm{M}}}$ and $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{mp}}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{RT}}{\mathrm{M}}}$
Thus $\mathrm{v}_{\text {rms }}=\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}} \mathrm{v}_{\text {mp }}$

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I
List-II

options.A:
AC generator
(I) Detects the presence of current in the circuit
options.B:
Galvanometer
(II) Converts mechanical energy into electrical energy
options.C:
Transformer
(III) Works on the principle of resonance in AC circuit
options.D:
Metal detector
(IV) Changes an alternating voltage for smaller or greater value
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :-
(A) (A)-(II), B-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
(B) (A)-(II), B-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
(C) (A)-(III), B-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

Official Ans. by NTA (A)

questions.text: A long straight wire with a circular crosssection having radius R , is carrying a steady current I. The current I is uniformly distributed across this cross-section. Then the variation of magnetic field due to current I with distance r $(\mathrm{r}<\mathrm{R})$ from its centre will be :-

options.D:
$\mathrm{B} \propto \frac{1}{\mathrm{r}}$

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol. Use Ampere's law
$$\text { B. } 2 \pi \mathrm{r}=\mu_{0} \cdot \frac{\mathrm{I}}{\pi \mathrm{R}^{2}} \cdot \pi \mathrm{r}^{2}$$

Thus $\mathrm{B} \propto \mathrm{r}$

questions.text: The electric field in an electromagnetic wave is given by $\mathrm{E}=56.5 \sin \omega(\mathrm{t}-\mathrm{x} / \mathrm{c}) \mathrm{NC}^{-1}$. Find the intensity of the wave if it is propagating along x -axis in the free space. (Given $\varepsilon_{0}=8.85 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{C}^{2} \mathrm{~N}^{-1} \mathrm{~m}^{-2}$ )

options.D:
$56.5 \mathrm{Wm}^{-2}$

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol. $\mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2} \varepsilon_{0} \mathrm{E}_{0}^{2} \mathrm{c}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2} \times\left(8.85 \times 10^{-12}\right)(56.5)^{2} \times\left(3 \times 10^{8}\right) \\
=4.24 \mathrm{Wm}^{-2}
\end{array}$$

questions.text: The two light beams having intensities I and 9I interfere to produce a fringe pattern on a screen. The phase difference between the beams is $\frac{\pi}{2}$ at point P and $\pi$ at point Q . Then the difference between the resultant intensities at P and Q will be :

options.D:
7 I

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol.
$$\begin{array}{l}
I_{P}=I+9 I+2 \sqrt{I \times 9 I} \cos \frac{\pi}{2} \\
I_{P}=10 I \\
I_{Q}=I+9 I+2 \sqrt{I \times 9 I} \cos \pi \\
=10 I-6 I=4 I \\
\therefore I_{P}-I_{Q}=10 I-4 I=6 I
\end{array}$$

questions.text: A light wave travelling linearly in a medium of dielectric constant 4, incident on the horizontal interface separating medium with air. The angle of incidence for which the total intensity of incident wave will be reflected back into the same medium will be (Given : relative permeability of medium $\mu_{\mathrm{r}}=1$ )

options.D:
60°

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)
Sol. For total internal reflection, $\mathrm{i}>\theta_{\mathrm{C}}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow \sin \mathrm{i}>\sin \theta_{\mathrm{C}} \\
\Rightarrow \sin \mathrm{i}>\frac{\mu_{\mathrm{R}}}{\mu_{\mathrm{D}}}
\end{array}$$

Also $\mu=\sqrt{\mu_{\mathrm{r}} \epsilon_{\mathrm{r}}}$
$$\frac{\mu_{\mathrm{R}}}{\mu_{\mathrm{D}}}=\frac{\sqrt{1 \times 1}}{\sqrt{4 \times 1}}=\frac{1}{2}$$

From (1), $\sin \mathrm{i}>\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{i}>30^{\circ}, \mathrm{i}=60^{\circ}$

questions.text: The ratio for the speed of the electron in the $3^{\text {rd }}$ orbit of $\mathrm{He}^{+}$to the speed of the electron in the $3^{\text {rd }}$ orbit of hydrogen atom will be :-

options.D:
$2: 1$

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)
Sol. $\quad \mathrm{v} \propto \frac{\mathrm{Z}}{\mathrm{n}} \propto \mathrm{Z}(\mathrm{n}=$ constant $)$
$$\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{He}^{*}}}{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{H}}}=\frac{\mathrm{Z}_{\mathrm{He}^{*}}}{\mathrm{Z}_{\mathrm{H}}}=\frac{2}{1}$$

questions.text: The difference of speed of light in the two media A and $\mathrm{B}\left(\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{A}}-\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}}\right)$ is $2.6 \times 10^{7} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. If the refractive index of medium B is 1.47, then the ratio of refractive index of medium $B$ to medium A is : (Given : speed of light in vacuum $\mathrm{c}=3 \times 10^{8} \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ )

options.D:
0.12

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)

Sol. $\quad \mathrm{v}=\frac{\mathrm{c}}{\mu}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow v_{B}=\frac{3 \times 10^{8}}{1.47}=2.04 \times 10^{8}=20.4 \times 10^{7} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\
\because v_{A}-v_{B}=2.6 \times 10^{7} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\
\therefore v_{A}=(20.4+2.6) \times 10^{7}=23 \times 10^{7} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\
\therefore \frac{\mu_{B}}{\mu_{A}}=\frac{v_{A}}{v_{B}}=\frac{23 \times 10^{7}}{20.4 \times 10^{7}}=1.13
\end{array}$$

questions.text: A teacher in his physics laboratory allotted an experiment to determine the resistance (G) of a galvanometer. Students took the observations for $\frac{1}{3}$ deflection in the galvanometer. Which of the below is true for measuring value of G?

options.A: $\frac{1}{3}$ deflection method cannot be used for determining the resistance of the galvanometer.
options.B: $\frac{1}{3}$ deflection method can be used and in this case the G equals to twice the value of shunt resistance(s).
options.C: $\frac{1}{3}$ deflection method can be used and in this case, the G equals to three times the value of shunt resistance(s)
options.D:
$\frac{1}{3}$ deflection method can be used and in this case the G value equals to the shunt resistance(s).

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol. In galvanometer
$$\Rightarrow\left(\mathrm{I}-\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{g}}\right) \mathrm{S}=\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{g}} \mathrm{G}$$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\frac{I_{g}}{I}=\frac{S}{S+G} \\
\Rightarrow \frac{1}{3}=\frac{S}{S+G} \Rightarrow S+G=3 S \Rightarrow G=2 S
\end{array}$$
